text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav Supreme Defence Council decides to keep a part of the Yugoslav army in the area bordering Albania on alert.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic amnesties a number of prisoners on occasion of Serbia National Day.
- Serbian government decides to immediately start drafting the project of Serbia's development up to 2010 with prospects for 2020.

- It is realistic to expect Yugoslav-Bulgarian trade to reach half a billion dollars in the long term, said president of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce Vlajko Stojiljkovic during talks with Bulgarian guests.
- Zastava car manufacturer still seeking foreign partner, says president Srboljub Vasovic.
- The fact that the new privatisation law is not binding is its main fault, says Democratic Party during talks with Serbia's economic and ownership transformation minister Milan Beko.
- Construction of Belgrade ring road starts Friday.
NASA BORBA
- Belgrade university held elections for first student parliament.
- Group of 17 independent economists urge speedy privatisation.
- U.N. Human Rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn says new Serbian information law will not contribute to liberalisaton of the media and calls for its re-examination.
- BK Television to sue official of the Socialist Party of Serbia Dusan Matkovic for claiming it is responsible for the maintenance of the outer-wall of sanctions against Yugoslavia.
- Pristina district prosecutor indicts 15 more Kosovo Albanians for terrorism.
- Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic promises that outstanding disability benefits for war invalids will be paid in the next four months.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Serbian Presidential elections will probably be in September, says president of Democratic Party Zoran Djindjic who expects President Slobodan Milosevic to run for a post in the federal state.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Kosovo Albanians open fire on policeman in Glogovac on Thursday evening, no one was injured, perpetrators flee.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Montenegro's interests lie in full contribution to Yugoslavia, says Montenegrin government press release.
- Montenegrin government promises 7 million dinars for the construction of a new Serbian Orthodox Church in Podgorica.
- There is an alternative way for Montenegro but when the ruling DPS loses power, says Liberal Alliance.
- Podgorica municipality budget is worth 86.2 million dinars.
